labs.verificationSystem: Every genuine certificate carries a task number + QR code; anyone can enter it at public.janoshik.com (no login) and get the archived, unalterable report. Has directly caught doctored certificates.
labs.reputationNotes: The de-facto standard, most-referenced third-party tester in the English-speaking research-peptide community. Trusted for blind-testing culture and high volume. HONESTY: NOT ISO 17025 accredited — vendor sites falsely claim it is; community trusts it as the best available option in an unregulated market, not regulatory-grade QC. Stated error margins ~5% (oils/orals) up to ~10% (liquid suspensions). Registered Oct 2022, founder Peter Magic.

labs.reputationNotes: Conventional contract analytical lab (nutraceutical/supplement/pharma) that also tests peptides; pharmaceutical-grade rigor, US-domestic. HONESTY: ISO/IEC 17025:2017 (No. 86258, PJLA) documented in Contract Laboratory directory + multiple sources, but NOT directly verified against PJLA scope DB; unconfirmed whether the specific RP-HPLC peptide assay is within accredited scope (17025 scope is method-specific).

proves: Identity of the specific submitted sample — which compound it actually is (mass spec; with MS/MS, sequence).
Purity of that one sample — % named compound vs impurities (HPLC-UV, within ~5% method error).
Content / quantification (mg active) ONLY when a quantification test was ordered.
That the certificate is authentic and unaltered — but only when its number resolves on the lab's public portal (defeats forged COAs).
That the tested tube was not an obvious mislabel — reputable labs catch this.
doesNotProve: That every vial/batch the vendor SHIPS matches the tested sample — only one submitted sample was analyzed; a vendor can cherry-pick (no chain of custody from batch to buyer).
Sterility, endotoxin, heavy metals, residual solvents, pH, or biological activity — excluded from a standard purity/identity COA unless separately ordered.
Regulatory or pharmaceutical grade — a COA from a non-ISO-17025 lab (incl. Janoshik, MZ Biolabs) is not FDA/EMA-accepted or court-grade, not GMP QC.
That the product is still at certified purity after shipping, temperature exposure, or storage time (no stability guarantee).
That an accreditation logo covers the specific assay — ISO 17025 scope is method-specific.
coaMeaning.iso17025Meaning: ISO/IEC 17025 is the international standard for the technical competence of testing labs: an independent body (PJLA, UKAS, ANAB, A2LA) audits people, equipment calibration, method validation, impartiality and quality system — but only for the specific methods in the accredited scope. It's the rigor regulators and courts accept, which is why it matters that most gray-market peptide testers (Janoshik, MZ Biolabs) do NOT hold it and operate as harm-reduction services, not regulatory labs.
